findings.issue_text: [High/data] The new OR condition deletes every WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method or scheduled date, allowing non-SMS reminders to be deleted
[Medium/concurrency] Updating retryCount using a stale previously-read value plus one can lose increments when workers overlap; the update should use Prisma's atomic increment operation
[Medium/bug] The retryCount update inside the catch block can itself throw, escaping the handler and preventing remaining reminders from being processed

[Medium/data] The broad catch treats database failures after successful SMS provider scheduling as delivery failures, leaving the reminder locally unscheduled and risking duplicate delivery or deletion at the retry limit

goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] The retryCount update inside the catch block can itself throw, escaping the handler and preventing remaining reminders from being processed

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that inside the catch block (lines 188-195), there's a prisma.workflowReminder.update() call that is not wrapped in a try-catch. If this database operation fails, it will throw an exception that escapes the outer try-catch block. Since this code is inside a loop processing multiple reminders (the for loop iterating over unscheduledReminders), an unhandled exception would prevent remaining reminders from being processed. This is a real bug - the error handling code itself can fail and break the processing loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] The broad catch treats database failures after successful SMS provider scheduling as delivery failures, leaving the reminder locally unscheduled and risking duplicate delivery or deletion at the retry limit

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a catch block (lines 186-194) that increments retryCount for any error during the SMS scheduling process. Looking at the try block, the SMS is scheduled first via twilio (scheduledSMS = await twilio.scheduleSMS), and then the database is updated to mark it as scheduled. If the database update fails after the SMS was successfully scheduled with Twilio, the catch block will increment retryCount. This means: 1) The SMS was actually scheduled with Twilio but the local DB doesn't reflect this, 2) On retry, the same SMS could be scheduled again with Twilio, 3) If retryCount exceeds 1, the reminder gets deleted (per the deletion logic at lines 31-44). This is a real bug where database failures after successful SMS scheduling lead to incorrect state.
